❑ More
あ t 으 means “more,” “else,” “in addition” and sometimes “other.” It is placed in front of
numbered things in the following ways. It is okay to add は after あ t 으.

Example Q&A
1. あ t 으 い k ら ですか。
   How much more is it?

   あ t 으 ご ひゃく えん です。
   It’s five hundred yen more.

2. あ t 으 は ど こ の resutoran が おいしいですか。
   What other restaurant is delicious?

   わたし の hoteru の resutoran が おいしいです。
   The restaurant in my hotel is delicious.

Example Conversations
1. Conversation between friends.
   A: なにが すきですか。                                 What do you like?
   B: すし と piza が すきです。                         I like sushi and pizza.
   A: あ t 으 、 なにが すきですか。                     What else do you like?
   B: あ t 으 は 、 さしみが すきです。                   In addition, I like sashimi.

2. Conversation between friends.
   A: あ t 으 は なにが いいですか。                     What else would you like?
   B: みず と supu-n を ください。                        Some water and a spoon, please.
   A: は い しょうしょう おまちください。                  Please wait a few moments.


11 Q&A しつもん と こたえ E→J

1. How many cups are there?                          Koppu は いくつ ですか。
   There are five cups.                                Koppu は いつつ です。
   There is one.                                       ひとつ です。

2. How many oranges are there?                       Orenji は なんこ / いくつ ですか。
   There are six oranges.                              Orenji は ろっこ / むっつ です。
   There are three.                                    みっつ です。 / さんこ です。

11 Q&A しつもん と こたえ J→E

1. Karenda- は なんまい ですか。                       How many calendars are there?
   ななじゅういちまい です。                             There are 71.
   Hya く にじゅうごまい です。                        There are 125.
   いちまん よんせんまい です。                          There are 14,000.

2. Ko-ra は なんぼん ですか。                          How many colas are there?
   はっぽん です。                                      There are eight.
   よんほん です。                                      There are four.

3. Ko-ra は あ t 으 なんぼん ですか。                  How many more cans of cola?
   あ t 으 ろっぽん ください。                          Six more cans, please.
   あ t 으 いっぽん ください。                          One more can, please.

4. あ t 으 は いくつ が いいですか。                  How many more would you like?
   あ t 으 ふたつ ください。                            Two more, please.
   あ t 으 じゅうろっこ ください。                      Sixteen more, please.

5. Banana は なんぼん ですか。                         How many bananas are there?
   じゅうごほん です。                                  There are 15.
   たぶん ろっぽん です。                               Maybe there are six.

6. Piza は なんまい ほしい ですか。                    How many pieces pizzas do you want?
   さんまい ほしい です。                               I want three.
   Piza は ほしくない です。                            I don't want any pizza.

   B: Okay.
   A: Oh! Two more tickets, please.
   B: Okay. Seven, right?
   A: No, that's wrong. Six tickets, please.

   B: はい。
   A: あっ、あ t 으 にまい ください。
   B: はい。ななまい ですね。
   A: いいえ、ちがいます。chiketto を ろくまい ください。

2. Conversation at a drink stand at the beach
   A: Please give me some cola.
   B: How many?
   A: Two, please.

   B: なんぼん ですか。
   A: にほん ください。

Hiragana: The Next Step

Congratulations on learning hiragana!
Here are some tips to help you reinforce what you have learned:

Let's put hiragana in our daily lives!
Write words in hiragana on “post it” notes and then stick them on items around your house.
You can even write しお and こしょう on your salt and pepper shakers using a permanent
marker. This will enforce your skills even when you aren't thinking about it.

[Image of chair with note reading いす]
[Image of calculator with note reading けいさんき]
[Image of cat with note reading ねこ]

Read manga!
Some manga (Japanese comics) and children's books will have small hiragana next to any
kanji used in dialogue. When hiragana is used in this way it is called “furigana”. Look for
furigana when purchasing manga to help you study. It's like Japanese on training wheels!

[Image of waitress with speech bubble containing 何(なに)を飲(の)む？]

Keep on learning!
Your next step is to learn katakana! You have come this far, so keep up the momentum.
We are sure you will also enjoy learning katakana in “Japanese From Zero!” Book 2.

11 Lesson Activities

❑ Japanese questions
Answer the following questions as if they were being asked to you directly. Write all the
answers in hiragana (except for the katakana words).

1. うま の あし は なんぼん ですか。

2. Amerika の はた の ほし は なんこ ですか。

3. えんぴつ が なんぼん ほしい ですか。

4. Piza が なんまい ほしい ですか。


❑ English questions
Translate then answer the following questions in Japanese. Write all your answers in
hiragana.

1. How many white stars are there? [Image of stars: white, white, black, black, white, white]

2. How many pencils are there? [Image of 8 pencils]

3. How many fingers are there? (including thumbs!) [Image of 2 hands]

4. How many flags are there? [Image of 6 flags]
